rules.title: Tenant Protection Act rent cap
rules.requirement: Owners may not raise rent more than 5% plus the local CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period, and no more than twice in that period. New tenancies may start at any rent.
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower
rules.effective_date_note: Original TPA rent cap effective 2020-01-01 (applies to increases from 2019-03-15; mobilehomes 2021-02-18). Current version (SB 567) effective 2024-01-01, operative 2024-04-01 per the statute text; repealed 2030-01-01.
rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted/subsidized affordable housing; dormitories; housing under stricter local rent control; certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years; separately alienable property (single-family, condos) not owned by REIT/corporation/corporate-member LLC with notice; owner-occupied duplex.
rules.penalty: Civil action for injunctive relief, overcharge damages (up to 3x if willful), attorney's fees; AG, city attorney or county counsel may enforce.
rules.interaction: Does not apply to housing under local rent control that limits annual increases to less than the state cap; does not expand or limit local authority under Civ. Code ch. 2.7 (Costa-Hawkins).

unverifiable_exemptions: single-family homes and condos not owned by REIT, corporation or corporate-member LLC

rules.conflict_note: Does not apply where stricter local rent control (e.g., LA RSO, SF, Berkeley, Santa Ana) covers the unit.

rules.title: Tenant Protection Act just cause eviction and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: After a tenant has lived in a unit 12 months (24 months if adult tenants were added), the owner may end the tenancy only for a stated at-fault or no-fault just cause. For no-fault reasons the owner must pay one month's rent in relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent, and the notice must say so.
rules.quoted_span: after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy
rules.key_value: Just cause after 12 months; no-fault relocation = 1 month's rent
rules.effective_date_note: Original TPA effective 2020-01-01 (the text references leases terminating on or after 2020-01-01 and July 1, 2020 notices). Current text operative 2024-04-01 per subd. (m); AB 1529 amendment effective 2026-01-01; repealed 2030-01-01.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels; nonprofit hospital/religious/care facilities; dormitories; owner shares bathroom/kitchen; owner-occupied single-family and duplex; certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years; separately alienable property owned by non-REIT/corporation with notice; deed-restricted affordable housing.
rules.penalty: Noncompliant notice void; actual damages, attorney's fees, up to 3x if willful; AG/city attorney/county counsel may seek injunction.
rules.interaction: Does not apply where a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before 9/1/2019, or a later more protective one, applies; property cannot be subject to both.

unverifiable_exemptions: single-family homes/condos separately owned by non-corporate owner with notice
dormitories, hospitals, care facilities, transient hotels

rules.conflict_note: Yields to local just-cause ordinances (e.g., LA, SF, Berkeley, Santa Ana, San Diego) that are earlier or more protective.

rules.title: Security deposit cap and return rules (AB 12 / AB 414)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not demand or receive security over one month's rent (two months for qualifying small landlords with no more than two properties and four units, except for service-member tenants). The deposit must be returned with an itemized statement within 21 days after the tenant vacates; photos are required.
rules.quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords)
rules.effective_date_note: Cap applies to security collected on or after 2024-07-01 (AB 12) per subd. (c)(6); current text amended by AB 414 effective 2026-01-01; photo requirement for tenancies beginning on/after 2025-07-01.
rules.exemptions: Two-month cap for natural-person/natural-person-LLC landlords owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units total; not for service members. Six months' advance rent allowed for leases of six months or longer.
rules.penalty: Bad faith retention: statutory damages up to twice the deposit plus actual damages.

coverage.landlord_size_condition: Two-month cap only for natural person/LLC of natural persons owning no more than 2 properties with no more than 4 units total
unverifiable_exemptions: small landlord status for two-month cap

rules.title: Application screening fee limits
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge a screening fee only up to actual out-of-pocket costs and time, never more than $30 per applicant (CPI-adjusted since 1998). No fee if no unit is available; landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund unused amounts, provide the credit report within 7 days, and offer first-come screening or refund to unselected applicants.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant
rules.key_value: $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted since 1998 (Berkeley states $68.96 for 2026)
rules.effective_date_note: Date of the AB 1170 amendment of the current text; the cap itself dates from earlier versions (CPI adjustment from 1998).
rules.conflict_note: The statute gives only the $30 base, not the current CPI-adjusted figure; the Berkeley Rent Board page (D005) states $68.96 for 2026, with no single official statewide figure.

rules.title: FEHA source-of-income protections (incl. SB 329, SB 267)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate against or harass applicants or tenants based on source of income, including Section 8 and HUD-VASH vouchers. For subsidized tenants, income standards must be based on the tenant's rent portion and applicants must be allowed to offer alternative evidence instead of credit history.
rules.quoted_span: For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person.
rules.key_value: ban on source-of-income discrimination incl. Section 8 and HUD-VASH vouchers
rules.effective_date_note: SB 329 added government subsidies to source of income effective 2020-01-01 (per D015); SB 267 amendment effective 2024-01-01 (HUD-VASH, credit-history provisions).
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied home renting to one additional person; shared living areas; senior housing.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied home renting to one additional person

rules.title: Civil Rights Council criminal history regulations (housing)
rules.requirement: Landlords may check criminal history but may not use blanket bans on people with a criminal record or consider arrests without conviction, sealed/expunged or juvenile records. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to being a good tenant or safety.
rules.citation: Cal. Code Regs. tit. 2, § 12264 et seq.
citation_aliases: Civil Rights Council criminal history regulations
rules.quoted_span: Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
rules.key_value: no blanket criminal-history bans; no consideration of arrests without conviction
rules.effective_date_note: Per D015 the regulations took effect Jan. 1, 2020. The regulation section is not stated in the documents; the citation is inferred.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied home renting to one additional person

rules.conflict_note: Citation inferred; documents do not cite the regulation section.

rules.title: Cartwright Act common pricing algorithm prohibition (AB 325 / SB 763)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to influence prices) as part of a restraint of trade, or to use or distribute one while coercing others to adopt its recommended prices. Applies to rental housing pricing software; single-firm tools using only own data are not covered.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter
rules.key_value: ban on common pricing algorithms using competitor data for collusion or coercion
rules.effective_date_note: Chaptered 2025-10-06 (D022); D028 states the laws took effect 2026-01-01.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any person using or distributing a common pricing algorithm; not limited to housing.
rules.exemptions: End consumers; algorithms using only a business's own data.
rules.penalty: Criminal fines up to $6M (corporations) / $1M (individuals) or twice gain/loss; civil fines up to $1M in AG/DA actions; treble damages and fees in private suits (per D028).

parsed.notes: Consolidated 14 candidates into 7 state records (one per law per category). The CA screening-fee statute states only the $30 base; the $68.96 figure appears only on a Berkeley page. FEHA source-of-income records (c17, c23, c85, c86) were merged into one § 12955 record. The criminal-history regulations were kept separate, with an inferred citation. Link-only sources D018-D021 only mirror statutes that are already covered.
